subject: Preserve synchronous Actor::Instruct epilogue semantics
description: DONE. The script-synchronous InstructOwner path translated commands and published the selected order, but omitted Original Actor::Instruct's accepted mmotionState=IN_PROGRESS write and ignored command dispatchers' pointer-changing terminal barrier. This could leave accepted WAIT-priority work reporting an older motion result, while a naive unconditional fix would overwrite authentic terminal results. Synchronous owner dispatch now propagates OwnerActionBarrier through movement, Seek, QuitSwordfight, smalltalk, turn/attention/wait, parry, position assertion, swordfight entry, and damage translators: source-explicit SetState exits return Skip before the shared epilogue, while accepted work publishes mpOrder and stamps IN_PROGRESS regardless of the element's final Rust state. The latter distinction preserves Original's accepted empty-order behavior, where motion is stamped before an element is subsequently terminated. Fifteen focused synchronous regressions cover accepted, replacement, blocked, redundant, inactive, and terminal branches; the manager-phase motion-edge and satisfied-entry regressions remain green.
